title: PresenceResource local-admin rejects real UDP [::1]:port hostinfo
description:
File: python/src/lichen/coap/resources/presence.py (_peer_is_local_admin, render_put)

The ixev write gate treats loopback as LCI admin. The helper only strips a port when hostinfo has exactly one colon (IPv4 host:port). IPv6 with a port is left intact, then strip("[]") turns "[::1]:54321" into "::1]:54321", which IPv6Address rejects, so the peer is untrusted.

aiocoap udp6 hostinfo is hostportjoin(plainaddress, sockaddr[1]) and omits the port only when it equals 5683. A loopback LCI client uses an ephemeral source port, so request.remote.hostinfo is "[::1]:<ephemeral>" on the real UDP path (bind_coap_udp defaults to ::1). LichenRemote.authority also emits "[host]:port" when the port is not 5683.

Impact:
- PUT /presence from a real loopback LCI client returns 4.01 unless allow_writes=True.
- Tests only use SimpleNamespace(hostinfo="[::1]") without a port, so they do not catch this.
- Fail-closed (not an auth bypass), but the documented LCI exception never matches production remotes.

Same parse mistake as open bead project-LICHEN-worker6-1v6y in messaging.py. confessions.py _host_from_hostinfo already parses bracketed IPv6 correctly. Do not refile 1v6y; this is the copy used by the presence write gate.
acceptance_criteria: PUT /presence from a loopback remote whose hostinfo is [::1]:<ephemeral> (and LichenRemote [::1]:non-5683) returns 2.04 without allow_writes. Mesh/global remotes still return 4.01. Tests cover the port-bearing IPv6 hostinfo form, not only [ ::1 ].
close_reason: Fixed strict aiocoap hostinfo parsing for bracketed IPv6 and IPv4 loopback peers with validated ports; added remote, scoped, malformed, and boundary regressions. Full CoAP suite, Ruff, and focused mypy are green.
